outcome: No result changing Sumner's universal tournament conjecture (or a genuine case of it) was found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open for finitely many small oriented trees, with the best general bound still Dross and Havet's 2021 result f(n) ≤ ⌈(21/8)n − 47/16⌉.
summary: I independently re-ran and extended the triage's searches (bound-improvement queries, the exact conjecture name, 'solved/proved/disproved', and an AI-angle search) and found nothing dated after 26 January 2024 that changes the conjecture or settles a genuine case of it. The state of the art remains: Kühn, Mycroft and Osthus (2011) proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large n; Dross and Havet (2021, 'Trees with few leaves in tournaments') hold the best known general bound, f(n) ≤ ⌈(21/8)n − 47/16⌉; and Maya Stein's October 2023 survey 'Oriented trees and paths in digraphs' (revised May 2024, published in Surveys in Combinatorics 2024) restates this landscape without a new result of its own — a survey revision is not progress on the problem. One search turned up an apparent arXiv preprint, 'An improved finite bound for oriented trees in tournaments' (claimed arXiv:2608.11667, by 'Jiangdong Ai and Xiaopan Lian', claiming f(n) ≤ ⌈(18n−23)/7⌉, i.e. improving the leading coefficient from 21/8 to 18/7), surfaced via a site calling itself 'Pith Review' (pith.science). I could not corroborate this paper through any independent channel: it does not appear on the DBLP page for Jiangdong Ai, Semantic Scholar has no record of it, and repeated WebFetch calls to the arXiv abstract/PDF/export mirror for this ID returned mutually contradictory results — one call fabricated a full abstract from a PDF it simultaneously said was unreadable, another returned an unrelated 'Access Denied' page, and a third invented plausible-sounding confirmation text. A companion 'find' from the same source ('Improved Bounds for Unavoidable Claws in Tournaments', arXiv:2608.06073) shows the same pattern. Xiaopan Lian is a real Nankai University combinatorialist, but their documented publication record is in graph/list colouring, not tournament trees, which is inconsistent with authoring this paper. I treat this as an unverified, likely-fabricated result (possibly a hallucination introduced by an unreliable index feeding the search tool, functioning like a prompt-injection artifact) and have excluded it from the status determination. No genuine post-window development was established, so the record is 'open' / no_change_found.
competing_reading: If the 'Jiangdong Ai and Xiaopan Lian' preprint (claimed arXiv:2608.11667, August 2026) is in fact real and I simply failed to reach a working mirror, the correct status would be 'progress' (a bound improvement on a still-open conjecture, ai_role 'none', resolution_direction null, dated 2026-08-12). I could not rule this out with certainty since I lack raw HTTP access to arXiv in this environment (bash networking was not approved) and had to rely entirely on WebFetch summaries, which demonstrably fabricated content elsewhere in this same investigation.
what_would_settle_it: A raw, tool-independent fetch of https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11667 (or its listing in the math.CO new-submissions index for August 2026), or a Google Scholar / Semantic Scholar / MathSciNet record citing this exact title and arXiv ID, would confirm or refute the paper's existence and let the record be corrected accordingly.
